newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Sierra Leoneans in Lagos show support for attack.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leoneans in Lagos show support for attack.

text.p: Placard-carrying Sierra Leonean residents marched to their high commission (embassy) in Lagos on Tuesday to show support for a Nigerian-led attack on Freetown to restore ousted civilian President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah to office.
The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reported that the group said the May 25 coup that toppled Kabbah was a setback for the country.
"The guns which were bought for use in defence of the people are now being used against them," the group's leader Alpha Kallon said.
He said the plotters had used the pretext of the May 25 coup "to loot, escape justice, create ethnic division and engage in acts of savagery".

The group presented a six-point resolution to a diplomat at the embassy, saying they fully support any action taken by Nigeria and the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) to reinstate the elected government.

Nigerian-led forces bombarded Sierra Leone on Monday but the Nigerians were outnumbered at a hotel where fierce fighting ensued and a ceasefire had to be arranged by the International Committee of the Red Cross.

NAN said Nigerian military spokesman Colonel Godwin Ugbo told reporters in Lagos on Tuesday that Nigerians should not panic over reports coming from Sierra Leone. "Our troops there are safe," he said.
